newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT- TMM bonds recommended.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT- TMM bonds recommended.

text.p: Santander Investment on Friday recommended bonds issued by Mexican transporation company, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM).
-- It said it was maintaining its credit rating on the company.

-- "We now believe that TMM's bond look attractive relative to other Mexican corporates, with the shorter-term 2000 and 2003 bonds looking better than the 2006, the price of which jumped in line with improved market conditions," analyst Jim Garvey wrote.
-- He noted that with the focus on TMM's railroad subsidiary, the company's shipping business has largely become secondary.

-- "For fixed-income investors, however, the shipping business takes priority, because repayment of TMM's obligations is expected to derive almost exclusively from shipping, given our expectations of negligible cash flow from the railroad subsidiary for about five years," he said.

-- He said TMM's strategy of diverting several ships to regions other than in the Far East appeared to have paid off in the first quarter of 1997. "As shipments grew, average prices rose and the downward cycle of gross margins shifted directions."
-- He noted that on the negative side, TMM's strategy also included offering very favorable credit terms.

-- "Near-term risks for bondholders include a rating downgrade (although such a scenerio appears priced in), difficulty in maintaining the capacity/pricing levels achieved in the first quarter, declining cash levels, and the possibility of additional contributions from TMM to avoid dilution," he said.
